input.task: What is the main heading on this page?

provenance:
PR #19, after five ablation sweeps aborted while /healthz answered in ~0.2s throughout (support-matrix D18). /healthz is liveness only — it proved the process existed and nothing about whether the agent could take work, which is the operational question that was actually missing. This case pins the readiness contract as a TRANSITION rather than a status code: idle before a submission, busy with the submitted run's id while it executes, idle again afterwards. Asserting the sequence is the point — a `ready` hardcoded true passes any before/after check that only looks at an idle service, and a hardcoded false passes any check taken mid-run. Both are killed by requiring all three states from one run, plus the identity of active_run_id in the middle one. The busy sample is taken while the run genuinely holds the semaphore (the planner is stubbed to hold it for a fixed interval), and its promptness matters as much as its content: /readyz is served by the same event loop as the agent, so a fast busy answer is positive evidence the loop is not blocked while a run executes — one of the named open candidates in D18. No browser, no LLM call, $0.00.

`hold_seconds` was 3.0 until PR #20 round 4 review (R14): the graded contract is the idle->busy->idle TRANSITION, not the hold's duration, so a 3.0s hold was 1.0-1.5s more than coverage needed and counted as suite wall-clock waste (ADR-013 Decision 4). The sample is taken `min(1.0, hold/3)` seconds after submission, and that gap has to clear the real start-race — the time between the POST returning and the stubbed planner acquiring the semaphore, measured at 4.3-5.2ms typically across 15 in-process trials with one 62ms outlier (cold-interpreter, not a steady-state cost this deep into the suite). `hold_seconds: 2.0` gives a 0.667s sample gap, ~10x the worst outlier observed, and is derived from that margin rather than copied from `1.0` (the value review happened to measure passing) — the same defect in a smaller font, had it been copied instead of re-derived. Recovers ~1.0s of suite wall-clock (case cost 3.55s -> 2.51s) without narrowing the margin to the point review flagged as the actual risk.
